records.summary: Historical native-first control policy for internal form lowerers.
records.rationale: The control-design interview, WAI-ARIA research, and June 7 control-completeness calibration support native web controls plus Aurelia value/checked/select/class/style channels as the first-ring substrate. Rich APG widgets remain visible but deferred until their behavior and accessibility contracts are modeled; email/url/tel/password/search/time/datetime-local/month/week are now explicit native form-control affordances rather than hidden text variants, and email/url/tel also have first-ring display-link affordances.
guidance: Use the authored control-use inventory and the generated field-variety fixture when changing native text, numeric, select, choice and submit lowerers.

records.summary: App-builder generated identity source uses explicit caller/domain identity value kind instead of inferring identity type from seed records.
records.rationale: The first generated app-builder routed fixture typecheck caught string seed IDs flowing into a generated numeric identity constructor. App-builder now models identity value kind as explicit DomainEntities input for direct router-backed list/detail and DI state-class lowering, validates seed records against that value kind, and keeps route params string-valued at the router boundary.
guidance: Keep route params string-valued at the router boundary and stringify identity values for lookup until a richer identity policy proves necessary.
Do not infer identity type from one seed record. Any source lowerer that emits typed entity identities, seed-backed state, or identity lookup code should require explicit caller/domain identity kind.

Target-specific source-lowering preflight requirements should run only after coarse input readiness is ready; broad/default source-lowering discovery should remain a menu instead of becoming partial because caller inputs are absent.

When adding new identity-consuming source lowerers, thread the identity value kind through domain descriptors, materialization, input-contract detail, preflight, seed-record validation, generated source, generated fixtures, and contracts in one slice.
